prompt:
Research Canonical's official statement on how long an Ubuntu LTS release receives standard support, and how long with Ubuntu Pro / ESM. Cite Canonical's own page and quote the periods.

Output format (required):
For every claim you attribute to a source, write one line in exactly this form:
SOURCE: <full URL> | QUOTE: "<a sentence copied word-for-word from that page>" | CLAIM: <what you take it to show>
For anything the task asks about that you could not find a source for, write one line:
NO_SOURCE_FOUND: <what you could not find>
You can write normal explanation before or after these lines.

response.content:
Based on Canonical's official documentation, an Ubuntu LTS release receives 5 years of standard security maintenance. With an Ubuntu Pro subscription, this coverage is extended through Expanded Security Maintenance (ESM) for a total of 10 years. Additionally, a paid "Legacy add-on" can extend security maintenance and support to a total of 15 years.

SOURCE: https://ubuntu.com/about/release-cycle?product= | QUOTE: "LTS are released every two years and receive 5 years of standard security maintenance." | CLAIM: Ubuntu LTS releases receive 5 years of standard security maintenance.

SOURCE: https://ubuntu.com/about/release-cycle?product= | QUOTE: "ESM extends the life of LTS releases by providing 10 years of security updates for the 'Main' repository and also adds 10 years of security coverage for the 'Universe' repository." | CLAIM: Ubuntu Pro/ESM provides 10 years of security updates for Main and Universe repositories.

SOURCE: https://ubuntu.com/about/release-cycle?product= | QUOTE: "At the end of the 10 year ESM period, the Legacy add-on can be purchased to cover additional 5 years of the lifetime of Ubuntu LTS, giving a total of 15 years security maintenance and support for LTS releases." | CLAIM: The Legacy add-on extends coverage to a total of 15 years.

SOURCE: https://canonical.com/legal/ubuntu-pro-description | QUOTE: "End of Standard Support: a date (5 years after the Release Date) on which free standard security maintenance service for the Ubuntu Main repository of an Ubuntu LTS expires" | CLAIM: Standard support ends 5 years after the release date.

SOURCE: https://ubuntu.com/security/cves/about | QUOTE: "Ubuntu Long Term Support (LTS) releases get up to 15 years of security maintenance and support." | CLAIM: LTS releases can receive up to 15 years of security maintenance and support.
